readings.title: Diagnosing the Plague in the Dwelling
readings.subtitle: Quarantining and Removing the Unfit Stones
readings.text: [Leviticus 14:33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [34] <dq>“When you come into the land of Kena‛an, which <dn>I</dn> am giving you as a possession, and <dn>I</dn> put a plague of leprosy in a house in the land of your possession,</dq> [35] <dq>then shall the one who owns the house come and inform the priest, saying, ‘It seems to me that there is some plague in the house.’</dq> [36] <dq>“And the priest shall command, and they shall empty <dn>את</dn> the house, before the priest goes in to look at the plague, so that all that is in the house is not made unclean. And after that the priest goes in to look at the house.</dq> [37] <dq>“And he shall look at the plague and see, if the plague is on the walls of the house with sunken places, greenish or reddish, which appear to be deep in the wall,</dq> [38] <dq>then the priest shall go out of the house, to the door of the house, and shut up the house seven days.</dq> [39] <dq>“And the priest shall come again on the seventh day and look and see, if the plague has spread on the walls of the house,</dq> [40] <dq>then the priest shall command, and they shall remove <dn>את</dn> the stones with the plague in them, and they shall throw them outside the city, into an unclean place,</dq> [41] <dq>while he lets <dn>את</dn> the house be scraped inside, all around, and the dust that they scrape off they shall pour out in an unclean place outside the city.</dq> [42] <dq>“And they shall take other stones and put them in the place of those stones, and take other mortar and plaster the house.</dq>

readings.title: The Verdict of Absolute Corruption
readings.subtitle: Dismantling the Irredeemable House
readings.text: [Leviticus 14:43] <dq>“And if the plague comes back and breaks out in the house, after he has removed the stones, after he has scraped the house, and after it is plastered,</dq> [44] <dq>then the priest shall come and look and see, if the plague has spread in the house, it is an active leprosy in the house, it is unclean.</dq> [45] <dq>“And he shall break down <dn>את</dn> the house, its stones, and its timber, and all the plaster of the house, and he shall bring them outside the city to an unclean place.</dq> [46] <dq>“And he who goes into the house, all the days while it is shut up, becomes unclean until evening.</dq> [47] <dq>“And he who lies down in the house has to wash his garments, and he who eats in the house has to wash his garments.</dq>

readings.title: The Restorative Atonement for the House
readings.subtitle: The Living Bird and the Cleansing Elements
readings.text: [Leviticus 14:48] <dq>“However, if the priest indeed comes in and looks at it and sees that the plague has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.</dq> [49] <dq>“And to cleanse the house, he shall take <dn>את</dn> two birds, and cedar wood, and scarlet, and hyssop.</dq> [50] <dq>“And he shall slay one of the birds in an earthen vessel over running water,</dq> [51] <dq>and he shall take <dn>את</dn> the cedar wood, and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the live bird, and dip them in the blood of the slain bird and in the running water, and shall sprinkle the house seven times.</dq> [52] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> shall thus cleanse the house with the blood of the bird and the running water and the live bird, and with the cedar wood, and with the hyssop, and with the scarlet,</dq> [53] <dq>and he shall let <dn>את</dn> the live bird loose outside the city in the open field, and shall make atonement for the house, and it shall be clean.</dq>

readings.title: The Complete Instruction for the Plague
readings.subtitle: Teaching the Distinction Between Fit and Unfit
readings.text: [Leviticus 14:54] <dq>“This is the Torah for any infection of leprosy, and eruption,</dq> [55] <dq>and for leprosy of a garment, and of a house,</dq> [56] <dq>and for a swelling, and for a scab, and for a bright spot,</dq> [57] <dq>to teach when it is unclean and when it is clean. This is the Torah of leprosy.”</dq>

readings.title: The Unfitness of a Bodily Discharge
readings.subtitle: The Spread of Disharmony to Vessels and Garments
readings.text: [Leviticus 15:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ěl, and say to them, ‘When any man has a discharge from his flesh, his discharge is unclean.</dq> [3] <dq>‘And this is his uncleanness in regard to his discharge; whether his flesh runs with his discharge, or his flesh is stopped up by his discharge, it is his uncleanness.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Any bed becomes unclean on which he who has the discharge lies, and any object on which he sits becomes unclean.</dq> [5] <dq>‘And anyone who touches his bed has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And he who sits on any object on which he who has the discharge sat, has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [7] <dq>‘And he who touches the flesh of him who has the discharge has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And when he who has the discharge spits on him who is clean, then he shall wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [9] <dq>‘Any saddle on which he who has the discharge rides becomes unclean.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And whoever touches any of that which was under him is unclean until evening. And he who is carrying them up has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And anyone whom he who has the discharge touches without rinsing his hands in water, shall wash his garments and bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And the earthen vessel which he who has the discharge touches has to be broken, and every wooden vessel has to be rinsed in water.</dq>

readings.title: The Atonement for Personal Restoration
readings.subtitle: Cleansing and the Economy of Sacrifice
readings.text: [Leviticus 15:13] <dq>‘And when he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count for himself seven days for his cleansing, and shall wash his garments, and shall bathe his flesh in running water, and be clean.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And on the eighth day he takes for himself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and shall come before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to the door of the Tent of Appointment, and shall give them to the priest.</dq> [15] <dq>‘And the priest shall prepare them, the one as a sin offering and the other as an ascending offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> because of his discharge.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And when a man has an emission of semen, then he shall wash all his flesh in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And any garment and any leather on which there is semen, shall also be washed with water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And when a woman lies with a man, and there is an emission of semen, they both shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq>

readings.title: The Appointed Time of Separation
readings.subtitle: Navigating Unfitness in the Monthly Cycle
readings.text: [Leviticus 15:19] <dq>‘And when a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her flesh is blood, she has to be in her separation for seven days. And whoever touches her is unclean until evening.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And whatever she lies on during her separation is unclean. And whatever she sits on is unclean.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And anyone who touches her bed has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And whoever touches any object that she sat on has to wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And if it is on the bed or on any object on which she sits, when he touches it, he is unclean until evening.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And if a man lies with her at all, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be unclean seven days. And any bed he lies on is unclean.</dq>

readings.title: Atonement for Prolonged Disharmony
readings.subtitle: Restoring Purity to Defend the Dwelling Place
readings.text: [Leviticus 15:25] <dq>‘And when a woman has a discharge of blood for many days, other than at the time of her monthly separation, or when she discharges beyond her usual time of monthly separation, all the days of her unclean discharge shall be as the days of her monthly separation. She is unclean.</dq> [26] <dq>‘Any bed on which she lies all the days of her discharge is to her as the bed of her monthly separation. And whatever she sits on is unclean, as the uncleanness of her monthly separation.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And anyone who touches them is unclean, and shall wash his garments, and shall bathe in water, and be unclean until evening.</dq> [28] <dq>‘But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count for herself seven days, and after that she is clean.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And on the eighth day she takes for herself two turtledoves or two young pigeons, and shall bring them to the priest, to the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [30] <dq>‘And the priest shall prepare the one as a sin offering and the other as an ascending offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the discharge of her uncleanness.</dq> [31] <dq>‘Thus you shall separate <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ěl from their uncleanness, lest they die in their uncleanness when they defile <dn>My</dn> Dwelling Place which is in their midst.</dq> [32] <dq>‘This is the Torah for one who has a discharge, and for him who emits semen and is unclean thereby,</dq> [33] <dq>and for her who is sick in her monthly separation, and for one who has a discharge, either man or woman, and for him who lies with an unclean woman.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Strict Protocol of the Set-Apart Place
readings.subtitle: The Linen Garments of the High Priest
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh after the death of the two sons of Aharon, as they drew near before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and died. [2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Mosheh, <dq>“Speak to Aharon your brother not to come in at all times to the Set-apart Place inside the veil, before <dn>את</dn> the lid of atonement which is on the ark, lest he die, because <dn>I</dn> appear in the cloud above the lid of atonement.</dq> [3] <dq>“With this Aharon should come into the Set-apart Place: with the blood of a young bull as a sin offering, and of a ram as an ascending offering.</dq> [4] <dq>“<dn>He</dn> should put on <dn>את</dn> the set-apart linen long shirt, with linen trousers on his flesh, and gird himself with a linen girdle, and be dressed with the linen turban – they are set-apart garments. And he shall bathe his body in water, and shall put them on.</dq> [5] <dq>“And from the congregation of the children of Yisra’ěl he takes <dn>את</dn> two male goats as a sin offering, and one ram as an ascending offering.</dq>

readings.title: Casting Lots for the Two Goats
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH’s Sacrifice and Azazel’s Relegation
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:6] <dq>“And Aharon shall bring <dn>את</dn> the bull as a sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house.</dq> [7] <dq>“And he shall take <dn>את</dn> the two goats and let them stand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> at the door of the Tent of Appointment.</dq> [8] <dq>“And Aharon shall cast lots for the two goats, one lot for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and the other lot for Azazel.</dq> [9] <dq>“And Aharon shall bring <dn>את</dn> the goat on which the lot for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell, and shall prepare it as a sin offering.</dq> [10] <dq>“But the goat on which the lot for Azazel fell is caused to stand alive before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to make atonement upon it, to send it into the wilderness to Azazel.</dq>

readings.title: The Cloud of Incense and the Blood of the Bull
readings.subtitle: Securing the Leader Before the Lid of Atonement
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:11] <dq>“And Aharon shall bring <dn>את</dn> the bull of the sin offering, which is for himself, and make atonement for himself and for his house, and shall slay <dn>את</dn> the bull as the sin offering which is for himself,</dq> [12] <dq>and shall take <dn>את</dn> a fire holder filled with burning coals of fire from the slaughter-place before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with his hands filled with sweet incense beaten fine, and shall bring it inside the veil.</dq> [13] <dq>“And he shall put <dn>את</dn> the incense on the fire before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the cloud of incense shall cover the lid of atonement which is on the Witness, lest he die.</dq> [14] <dq>“And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the lid of atonement on the east side, also in front of the lid of atonement he sprinkles some of the blood with his finger seven times.</dq>

readings.title: The Blood Atonement for the Assembly
readings.subtitle: Reconciling the Tent of Appointment
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:15] <dq>“And he shall slay <dn>את</dn> the goat of the sin offering, which is for the people, and shall bring its blood inside the veil, and shall do with that blood as he did with the blood of the bull, and sprinkle it on the lid of atonement and in front of the lid of atonement.</dq> [16] <dq>“And he shall make atonement for <dn>את</dn> the Set-apart Place, because of the uncleanness of the children of Yisra’ěl, and because of their transgressions in all their sins. And so he does for the Tent of Appointment which is dwelling with them in the midst of their uncleanness.</dq> [17] <dq>“And no man should be in the Tent of Appointment when he goes in to make atonement in the Set-apart Place, until he comes out. And he shall make atonement for himself, and for his household, and for all the assembly of Yisra’ěl.</dq> [18] <dq>“And he shall go out to the slaughter-place that is before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and make atonement for it. And he shall take some of the blood of the bull and some of the blood of the goat, and put it on the horns of the slaughter-place all around.</dq> [19] <dq>“And he shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and cleanse it, and set it apart from the uncleanness of the children of Yisra’ěl.</dq>

readings.title: Transferring the Crookedness of Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: Sending the Scapegoat into the Wilderness
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:20] <dq>“And when he has finished atoning for the Set-apart Place, and the Tent of Appointment, and the slaughter-place, he shall bring the live goat.</dq> [21] <dq>“Then Aharon shall lay both his hands on the head of the live goat, and shall confess over it <dn>את</dn> all the crookednesses of the children of Yisra’ěl, and all their transgressions in all their sins, and shall put them on the head of the goat, and shall send it away into the wilderness by the hand of a fit man.</dq> [22] <dq>“And the goat shall bear on itself all their crookednesses, to a land cut off. Thus he shall send the goat away into the wilderness.</dq>

readings.title: Washing and Ascending Offerings
readings.subtitle: Eliminating the Residue of the Sin Offering
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:23] <dq>“Aharon shall then come into the Tent of Appointment, and shall take off <dn>את</dn> the linen garments which he put on when he went into the Set-apart Place, and shall leave them there.</dq> [24] <dq>“And he shall bathe his body in water in the set-apart place, and shall put on <dn>את</dn> his garments, and shall come out and prepare his ascending offering and the ascending offering of the people, and make atonement for himself and for the people,</dq> [25] <dq>and burn <dn>את</dn> the fat of the sin offering on the slaughter-place.</dq> [26] <dq>“And he who sent away the goat to Azazel washes his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward he comes into the camp.</dq> [27] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> the bull for the sin offering and <dn>את</dn> the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the Set-apart Place, is brought outside the camp. And they shall burn their skins, and their flesh, and their dung with fire.</dq> [28] <dq>“And he who burns them washes his garments, and shall bathe his body in water, and afterward he comes into the camp.</dq>

readings.title: The Seventh Moon and the Day of Affliction
readings.subtitle: An Eternal Statute for National Rest and Purity
readings.text: [Leviticus 16:29] <dq>“And this shall be for you a law forever: In the seventh new moon, on the tenth day of the new moon, you afflict <dn>את</dn> your beings, and do no work, the native or the stranger who sojourns among you.</dq> [30] <dq>“For on that day he makes atonement for you, to cleanse you, to be clean from all your sins before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [31] <dq>“It is a Sabbath of rest for you, and you shall afflict <dn>את</dn> your beings – a law forever.</dq> [32] <dq>“And the priest, who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father’s place, shall make atonement, and shall put on <dn>את</dn> the linen garments, the set-apart garments,</dq> [33] <dq>and he shall make atonement for <dn>את</dn> the Most Set-apart Place, and make atonement for the Tent of Appointment and for the slaughter-place, and make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.</dq> [34] <dq>“And this shall be for you a law forever, to make atonement for the children of Yisra’ěl, for all their sins, once a year.”</dq> And he did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded Mosheh.
